meta.name: PoC 1 (A7): DPIR + MARL recovery on 1 x 4-sector + 6 x 2-sector N367 and 8 IP-50
meta.event: t0: the devices that die lose power at their switched PDU outlets: the hub (its AC PoE injector), CORE's two IP-50 radios, SRV-E2E and SRV-DPIR. The hub's six paths and the W1-CORE and CORE-E1 hops go down with them; nothing RF moves at t0 (fixed pads, no programmable attenuators). W1-W2 and E1-E2 unchanged. The bridges E2-W2, E1-N, W1-S (links between surviving nodes, on their fixed pads) are held down before t0 with Terragraph ignition disabled on the E2E controller (TG links link-E2-W2, link-E1-N, link-W1-S, names TBC). SRV-E2E is off after t0, so MARL engages a bridge at node level: the A-end node's agent PC sends tg2 minion assoc to its node (TBC on the N367 firmware; fallback: a standby E2E controller on BENCH-CTL). No RF change.

assumed: one 3.6 m x 0.8 m bench table to the right of the rack, top at 750 mm (estimate)

steps.title: Assemble the rack
steps.text: Build the StarTech 4POSTRACK42 (42U), set the rail-to-rail depth to 900 mm and level it. Make it stable before anything heavy goes in: lower the levelling feet until the castors are off the floor (or lock every castor) and fit the rack's stabiliser or floor anchor if one is supplied. Fit the rack earth bar (RACK-EARTH, grounding kit) on the left rear post with paint-piercing washers; it is bonded to the lab earth bar in the next step, before anything else goes in. Stack from U1 upwards, power at the bottom. Fit the M6 cage nuts with the cage-nut tool as each item goes in: 4 per front- or rear-mounted item, 72 for the items plus 2 per rear lacing bar (80 in all; front or rear posts as each step says; rail-kit servers, the UNIRAILS1U rails (own M5 hardware) and blanking panels need none).

steps.title: Cable: Earth bond
steps.text: Bond the rack earth bar (RACK-EARTH, left rear post) to the lab earth bar with B001: 6 mm2 green/yellow, 2-hole lug with paint-piercing washers at the rack bar, ring lug at the lab bar; crimp the lugs with the ring-lug crimper and torque them with the torque wrench to the value marked on each stud. Print two ID labels and tag both ends. Check it end to end with the multimeter on ohms, test leads nulled first (REL): under 0.1 ohm. From now on wear the ESD strap bonded to this earth.

steps.title: Mount the PDUs
steps.text: Fit the 3 switched PDUs at U1-U3 (1U each) on the REAR posts (4 cage nuts + screws each, at the rear), outlets and network port facing the rear. Commission each PDU bare, before any lead is fitted: plug its cord into its wall socket with nothing connected, enable front-panel outlet switching, set every outlet OFF and every outlet's power-on state to OFF (front panel or local port), check on its display that every outlet reads OFF, set its management address, then unplug the cord again. From here on the PDU cords stay out of the wall until power-up.

steps.title: Mount the DC drawers
steps.text: Rectifier shelves and distribution panels above the PDUs, on the front posts (ears on 4 cage nuts + screws each); the two rectifier shelves also run on a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails, bolted to the front and rear posts with the rail kit's own M5 cage nuts and screws. DC-RECT2 (U4) and DC-DIST2 (U5) give -48 V to the IP-50 radios; the DC-DIST2 RTN bus (= DC-RECT2 +V) is bonded to the rack earth bar (B002, first item of the DC cable step), which makes the -48 V system positive grounded, and bus B is strapped to bus A (D017). DC-RECT (U6) and DC-DIST (U7) give +48 V to the node adaptors and the Spider-box DCIN inputs; DC-RECT's output stays floating (not earthed). Every breaker (5 A or less) OFF, the DCD1M main / input breaker too if the panel has one; every GMT fuse OUT, bagged and labelled with its position until power-up. Label the fronts with the label printer: DC-RECT and DC-DIST '+48 V FLOATING - NODES', DC-RECT2 and DC-DIST2 '-48 V POSITIVE GROUND - IP-50': the two rectifier shelves are the same part, so the label is what tells them apart.

steps.title: Adaptor shelf
steps.text: Fit the 1U shelf at U8 on the front posts (4 cage nuts). Positions are measured from the left ear as seen from the FRONT (your right-hand ear when you stand at the rear). Rear row, left to right: PA-01 (node W1), PA-02 (node W2), PA-03 (node S), PA-04 (node N), PA-05 (node E1), PA-06 (node E2), INJ-HUB (node HUB); front row, at the far right, unwired spares PA-07 to PA-10. RJ45 and DC terminals face the rear; every body 10 mm or more from the next.

steps.title: Splitter tray (8 splitters)
steps.text: Fit the 1U tray at U9, directly under the Spider boxes (front posts, 4 cage nuts). Then, on a work surface and BEFORE any splitter goes onto the tray or any tray cable is laid, fit the 16 fixed pad stacks onto the 8 splitters in the hand (n = tile 1-4): SPL-HUBW.tn P1 takes PAD-HUB-W1.tn (20 + 8 dB), P2 PAD-HUB-W2.tn (20 + 3 dB); SPL-HUBE.tn P1 takes PAD-HUB-E1.tn (20 + 8 dB), P2 PAD-HUB-E2.tn (20 + 3 dB); the larger pad on the port, each pad's male nut onto the female port in front of it; read the value printed on each pad first. Hold the splitter body with the backing wrench and torque every joint to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m), the torque wrench's handle in the plane of the two stacks and pointing away from the other stack (jaws above and below the nut); P1's stack first, then P2's. The stacks end up 12 mm apart (about 2 mm between bodies); if they foul, fit P2's through a short SMA M-F adapter so its nuts stand beyond P1's (assumptions); never bend a stack. Then lay the 8 splitters flat, all the same way round: S to the LEFT, ports 1 and 2 with their stacks to the RIGHT (port 1 toward the front), label up; one column per split hub module, left to right SPL-HUBW (HUB.W), SPL-HUBE (HUB.E); rows front to back = tile 1-4; the stacks lie on the tray, up to 62 mm right of their splitter. The tile cables reach S from the left side lane. Cable lanes: every cable leaves its port or stack straight out; the port-2 stack's cable runs 8 mm further out than port 1's; each row further back rises 10 mm more before running forward, over the front rows' plugs.

steps.title: Spider boxes
steps.text: Mount the four 1U Spider boxes SB1 (top, U13) to SB4 (U10). Which box goes where: SB1 = GTS003 #1, serial SF06000007 (assumed); SB2 = GTST002B, serial SF06000001; SB3 = GTST003, serial SF06000058; SB4 = GTS003 #2, serial SF06000031 (assumed). Check the serial on each box's label before it goes in. For each box fit a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails first, bolted to the front AND rear posts with the M5 cage nuts and screws in the rail kit; slide the box onto them and fix its ears on 4 M6 cage nuts + screws at the front. Odd / even / hybrid is the Terragraph polarity the E2E controller gives each node (a software setting, not a label on the box): the same box can be odd in one PoC and even in the next. The module map of each front panel is in the close-ups that follow the table of this step. The boxes sit about 0.52-0.70 m off the floor: every IF joint (the pad stacks and their cables in the IF-link steps) is made down there, so work kneeling on a mat or from a low stool, with the torque wrench square to each joint. Hold point before any DCIN run is landed at its box: confirm what the green 4-pole DC header (DCIN) on each box's rear feeds, at what voltage, its pin order and polarity, and its pitch (the plug is in the parts list: 4-pole pluggable screw-terminal plug, Phoenix MSTB 2.5/4-STF class, pitch TBC). The design assumes the box fans and the Raspberry Pi at 48 V DC, fed from DC-DIST CB7-CB10 (D018-D021, SB1 on CB7; SB2 on CB8; SB3 on CB9; SB4 on CB10), landed at power-up only. Any other voltage or function: STOP; the DCIN runs stay unlanded and the design changes; if DCIN turns out to feed a node, that node's power path changes and SB2's feed must go on a switched PDU outlet (the hub dies at t0).

steps.title: Servers and traffic hosts
steps.text: Fit the rail kits shipped with each server (toolless in square holes) and slide the servers in one at a time, network ports at the back (sizes in the rack schedule). Never have more than one server pulled out on its rails at a time: the rack can tip. SRV-E2E and SRV-DPIR die at t0 on one switched outlet each: if one has two PSUs, REMOVE PSU 2 (and blank its bay) before it goes in.

steps.title: Switches, cable manager, agent shelf
steps.text: Cable manager at U14 (front posts), between AGENTS above and SB1 below; SW-DATA at U27 on the front posts, ports to the front, on a pair of UNIRAILS1U rails (front and rear posts, kit M5 hardware; Netgear's RBS1830 fits 18-30 in rails only); SW-OOB at U26 on the REAR posts, ports to the rear; GNSS splitter at U28, connectors to the rear; agent PCs on their shelf at U15-U16: back row with connectors to the rear, front row turned round with connectors to the FRONT, so no connector faces another PC; each PC's power brick is Velcroed to the rear lacing bar beside the shelf. Then fit 4 lacing bars on the rear posts (2 cage nuts each), power on the left and data on the right as seen from the front.

steps.title: Blanking panels
steps.text: Blank every empty U (toolless panels, no cage nuts).

steps.title: Bench table
steps.text: Place the bench table to the right of the rack and fit the cable bridge (CABLE-BRIDGE) from the rack's right post to the table's rack-side end, its floor at table height, divider in: data in the front compartment, power in the rear one. Set out the equipment at the positions in the table (every item 5 mm or more from the next): the operator station nearest the rack (keyboard at the front, monitor behind it, BENCH-CTL behind the monitor, the switched -48 V supplies beside BENCH-CTL) and the strip lengthwise just right of the monitor (610 mm from the rack-side end), inlet toward the back edge; the IP-50 radios in hop pairs, the two radios of a hop side by side with their waveguide flanges facing each other (W1-CORE: IP50-W1-CORE@W1 | IP50-W1-CORE@CORE, front row, left; CORE-E1: IP50-CORE-E1@CORE | IP50-CORE-E1@E1, back row, left; W1-W2: IP50-W1-W2@W1 | IP50-W1-W2@W2, front row, right; E1-E2: IP50-E1-E2@E1 | IP50-E1-E2@E2, back row, right), in a front and a back row 120 mm apart and two columns with a 150 mm aisle between them; the gap between the two radios of a hop takes the transitions, the pad stacks and the hop's one SMA cable (IP-50 chain step); no radio is stacked; the analyser at the far end; screw the table earth bar (TABLE-EARTH) to the table's back edge behind the aisle between the radio columns, studs up just below the top. Keep the back 110 mm of the table clear for the cable lanes: data bundle 70-110 mm from the back edge, power bundle within 30 mm of it; keep the aisle between the strip and the A-side radios clear.

steps.title: Cable: DC power and earth bonds
steps.text: 31 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. First the earth bonds and the -48 V system's own wiring, all made before any feed is landed: bond the DC-DIST2 RTN bus earth stud to the rack earth bar with B002 (6 mm2 green/yellow: positive ground); strap bus B to bus A with D017 (skip the strap if the panel ships strapped); bond the table earth bar to the rack earth bar with B004 (6 mm2, along the floor under the cable protector with the strip cord) and each IP-50 radio's chassis ground screw to its TABLE-EARTH stud with B005-B012 (2.5 mm2 green/yellow; ground screw position TBC); crimp the lugs with the ring-lug crimper, torque them with the torque wrench to the value marked on each stud, and check every bond end to end with the multimeter (leads nulled, under 0.1 ohm). Strip each end with the wire stripper and ferrule every stranded end (ferrule crimper). Conductor convention: before landing a run, shrink a red (+48 V) or blue (-48 V) sleeve onto the SUPPLY conductor at both ends with the heat gun (breaker or fuse output, or supply terminal); the unsleeved conductor is the 0 V return. Land each run at its breaker, fuse or supply end only and torque those terminals to the value marked on them (DCD1M, N250110) with the torque screwdriver; leave the LOAD end (adaptor DC terminal, Spider DCIN plug (Phoenix MSTB 2.5/4-STF class 4-pole plug for the green DC header, pitch TBC), radio DC plug) unlanded, tagged and taped with insulating tape: it is landed and torqued at the polarity check at power-up. The Spider DCIN runs (D018-D021, box fans / Pi) are landed at their breakers like the others; their box end stays unlanded until the hold point of step 7 has confirmed DCIN is a 48 V DC input and its pin order: then each run goes into the screw terminals of its 4-pole pluggable screw-terminal plug (the plug, not the green 4-pole DC header, takes the conductors). Rack runs go up the LEFT side of the rack as seen from the front (your right-hand side when you stand at the rear), on the rear lacing bars, 50 mm or more from coax and data. The IP-50 feeds are the exception: from DC-DIST2's front fuse outputs they run along the front of its U to the RIGHT side of the rack, back to about 640 mm behind the front rail and up to table height in their own wrapped power bundle, then cross in the REAR (power) compartment of the cable bridge. On the table every radio feed (the switched supplies' leads too) runs in the power lane along the back edge, 50 mm or more behind the data lane, and reaches its radio through the row gap and the aisles, away from the data cables. Bend radius 5 x the cable diameter or more; Velcro every 300 mm.

steps.title: Cable: PoE to the nodes
steps.text: 7 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Adaptor (or injector) RJ45 to the node ETH1 at the rack rear, down the LEFT side with the power cables (seen from the front). WARNING: Q cables carry 48 V DC on an ordinary RJ45 (passive PoE, power only): never plug one into a switch, PC or laptop; put a yellow '48 V PoE - NOT ETHERNET' flag next to the ID label at both ends. Velcro to the lacing bars every 300 mm, no zip ties; Cat6A bend radius 4 x diameter (about 30 mm) or more; coil slack on the lacing bar, never at the connector.

steps.title: Cable: AC mains
steps.text: 30 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Fit the lead at the device inlet and at its PDU outlet (or strip outlet) only. Do NOT plug the PDU cords or the strip cord into the wall: they stay unplugged until power-up (guide section 6), and every PDU outlet stays OFF. Rack mains runs go up the LEFT side of the rack as seen from the front, 50 mm or more from coax and data, Velcroed to the rear lacing bars. The leads of the switched -48 V supplies (PSU-W1-CORE@CORE, PSU-CORE-E1@CORE) leave the rack low on the RIGHT in their own wrapped power bundle (about 640 mm behind the front rail), 50 mm or more from the data bundle, and cross in the REAR (power) compartment of the cable bridge into the table's power lane. The strip cord runs from its wall socket along the floor under the cable protector to the rack-side table leg, up the leg at the back edge and along the power lane to the strip inlet. Servers switched at t0 (SRV-E2E, SRV-DPIR): ONE lead each, to PSU 1; PSU 2 was removed in the servers step (step 8).

steps.title: Cable: Data to SW-DATA
steps.text: 28 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Data runs up the RIGHT side of the rack as seen from the front (your left-hand side at the rear). Node SFP+ (rear) to SW-DATA (front): cross from the rear to the front on the right side at SW-DATA's U. The front-row agent PCs face the front: their data and management leads run along the front of the AGENTS shelf to the right side. Runs to the bench table leave the rack on the right at about 560 mm behind the front rail and cross in the FRONT (data) compartment of the cable bridge (CABLE-BRIDGE) into the table's data lane, 50 mm or more in front of the power lane. Clean every LC end with the one-click cleaner before mating. Bend radius: OM4 30 mm or more, DAC 50 mm or more, Cat6A 4 x diameter. Coil slack behind the cable manager, Velcro only.

steps.title: Cable: Management to SW-OOB
steps.text: 19 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Management runs up the RIGHT side as seen from the front. SW-OOB and the PDUs sit on the rear posts, so their runs stay at the rear; BENCH-CTL and the analyser come from the table's data lane through the front (data) compartment of the cable bridge and up the right side. The front-row agent PCs face the front: their data and management leads run along the front of the AGENTS shelf to the right side. Cat6A bend radius 4 x diameter; Velcro every 300 mm; slack on the lacing bars.

steps.title: Cable: GNSS
steps.text: 10 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. First the arrestor: fit GNSS-ARR on the wall where the antenna lead enters the room, just above the lab earth bar, and bond its ground lug to the lab earth bar with B003 (6 mm2 green/yellow, short and straight, no loops; ring lugs crimped and torqued) BEFORE the antenna lead is connected to anything; if the building already has an entry arrestor, bond to that instead (facilities). Then the antenna lead G001 to the arrestor's antenna side, and the jumper G009 from its equipment side up the wall and in along the rack's LEFT side (outside the rails) to GNSS-SPL's input at the rear of the rack top. Jumpers down the RIGHT side of the rack, just outside the rails about 450 mm behind the front rail (not the rear post), then in behind each Spider box to its node's GNSS SMA. Fit an ANNE-50+ load on every unused splitter output (GNSS-SPL.out8). RG-316 bend radius 25 mm or more, LMR-400 / LMR-240 per their data sheets. Torque the SMA joints to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, holding the jack with the backing wrench.

steps.title: Cable: Operator station
steps.text: 2 cables; print two ID labels per cable on the label printer and tag both ends before routing. Operator station on the table: video and USB between BENCH-CTL, the monitor and the keyboard, on the table top around the monitor; keep them clear of the strip and the power lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-W1 (20 + 8 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: HUB.W tile n (SB2.M1.Tn) to SPL-HUBW.tn S (fitted now, shared by HUB-W1 and HUB-W2); pad stack PAD-HUB-W1.tn on SPL-HUBW.tn P1, fitted in step 6 (20 dB + 8 dB = 28 dB, target 27.6 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); cable from the stack's OUT to W1.E tile n (SB1.M1.Tn). Make every tray joint in the hand, never on the tray: lift the splitter with its stacks a few centimetres off the tray, screw the cable's plug onto the stack's OUT (or onto S), hold the stack's outer pad (for S the splitter body) with the backing wrench and torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, then lay the splitter back in its place; never bend a stack or lever it against the tray or a fitted cable. HUB-W1 goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Route: from the stack's OUT the cable runs on to the right, turns toward the front at its lane (the port-2 stacks' lane 8 mm further right than port 1's; each row further back rises 10 mm more, over the front rows' plugs), runs along the tray front edge to the left side lane, up the side to the lower edge of SB1 (the seam with the unit below), in along that seam and up into the tile; never across the face of another box. The S cables (R001-R004) run from the hub tile straight out, down to the seam under SB2, left to the left side lane, down to the tray and in along the tray front, then back to S at the left end of each splitter. Connect in tile order, t1 (front row) first and t4 (back row) last. The four link cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-W2 (20 + 3 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: HUB.W tile n (SB2.M1.Tn) to SPL-HUBW.tn S (already fitted in step 19: R001-R004, shared); pad stack PAD-HUB-W2.tn on SPL-HUBW.tn P2, fitted in step 6 (20 dB + 3 dB = 23 dB, target 23.1 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); cable from the stack's OUT to W2.E tile n (SB1.M3.Tn). Make every tray joint in the hand, never on the tray: lift the splitter with its stacks a few centimetres off the tray, screw the cable's plug onto the stack's OUT (or onto S), hold the stack's outer pad (for S the splitter body) with the backing wrench and torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, then lay the splitter back in its place; never bend a stack or lever it against the tray or a fitted cable. HUB-W2 goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Route: from the stack's OUT the cable runs on to the right, turns toward the front at its lane (the port-2 stacks' lane 8 mm further right than port 1's; each row further back rises 10 mm more, over the front rows' plugs), runs along the tray front edge to the left side lane, up the side to the lower edge of SB1 (the seam with the unit below), in along that seam and up into the tile; never across the face of another box. Connect in tile order, t1 (front row) first and t4 (back row) last. The four link cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-E1 (20 + 8 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: HUB.E tile n (SB2.M2.Tn) to SPL-HUBE.tn S (fitted now, shared by HUB-E1 and HUB-E2); pad stack PAD-HUB-E1.tn on SPL-HUBE.tn P1, fitted in step 6 (20 dB + 8 dB = 28 dB, target 27.6 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); cable from the stack's OUT to E1.W tile n (SB4.M1.Tn). Make every tray joint in the hand, never on the tray: lift the splitter with its stacks a few centimetres off the tray, screw the cable's plug onto the stack's OUT (or onto S), hold the stack's outer pad (for S the splitter body) with the backing wrench and torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, then lay the splitter back in its place; never bend a stack or lever it against the tray or a fitted cable. HUB-E1 goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Route: from the stack's OUT the cable runs on to the right, turns toward the front at its lane (the port-2 stacks' lane 8 mm further right than port 1's; each row further back rises 10 mm more, over the front rows' plugs), runs along the tray front edge to the left side lane, passing in front of SPL-HUBW's column, up the side to the lower edge of SB4 (the seam with the unit below), in along that seam and up into the tile; never across the face of another box. The S cables (R005-R008) run from the hub tile straight out, down to the seam under SB2, left to the left side lane, down to the tray and in along the tray front, then back to S at the left end of each splitter. Connect in tile order, t1 (front row) first and t4 (back row) last. The four link cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-E2 (20 + 3 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: HUB.E tile n (SB2.M2.Tn) to SPL-HUBE.tn S (already fitted in step 21: R005-R008, shared); pad stack PAD-HUB-E2.tn on SPL-HUBE.tn P2, fitted in step 6 (20 dB + 3 dB = 23 dB, target 23.1 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); cable from the stack's OUT to E2.W tile n (SB4.M3.Tn). Make every tray joint in the hand, never on the tray: lift the splitter with its stacks a few centimetres off the tray, screw the cable's plug onto the stack's OUT (or onto S), hold the stack's outer pad (for S the splitter body) with the backing wrench and torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench, then lay the splitter back in its place; never bend a stack or lever it against the tray or a fitted cable. HUB-E2 goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Route: from the stack's OUT the cable runs on to the right, turns toward the front at its lane (the port-2 stacks' lane 8 mm further right than port 1's; each row further back rises 10 mm more, over the front rows' plugs), runs along the tray front edge to the right side lane, up the side to the lower edge of SB4 (the seam with the unit below), in along that seam and up into the tile; never across the face of another box. Connect in tile order, t1 (front row) first and t4 (back row) last. The four link cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-S (30 + 5 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: pad stack PAD-HUB-S.tn screwed onto HUB.S tile n (SB2.M3.Tn); cable from the stack's OUT to S.N tile n (SB3.M1.Tn). Fit the pad stacks first, straight out to the front: BW-S30W2+ (30 dB) on the tile, then BW-S5W2+ (5 dB) on it (30 dB + 5 dB = 35 dB, target 34.5 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); read the value printed on each pad first; each pad's male nut screws onto the female jack in front of it. Hold that jack with the backing wrench and torque every joint to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m). Each stack stands 62 mm proud of SB2's front and must not carry the cable: bend the cable down from the stack's OUT to the seam bundle at the unit's lower edge and strap it (Velcro) to that bundle, or to the cable manager, within 150 mm of the stack, then on to the side lane; never lever a stack sideways. HUB-S goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Then route every cable through the left side lane: down to the lower edge of its unit (the seam with the unit below), along it to the side of the rack, along the side and in along the lower edge of the other unit; never across the face of another box (every tile keeps 17 mm clear above and below its SMA; runs pass 15 mm or more in front). Connect tile 1 first; at the B tile torque to 8 in-lb with the backing wrench on the jack. If a seam bundle from an earlier step lies close to a tile, ease it aside by hand and fit the wrench sideways. The four cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link HUB-N (30 + 7 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: pad stack PAD-HUB-N.tn screwed onto HUB.N tile n (SB2.M4.Tn); cable from the stack's OUT to N.S tile n (SB3.M3.Tn). Fit the pad stacks first, straight out to the front: BW-S30W2+ (30 dB) on the tile, then BW-S7W2+ (7 dB) on it (30 dB + 7 dB = 37 dB, target 37.2 dB, the A7 'before' setting; pad schedule); read the value printed on each pad first; each pad's male nut screws onto the female jack in front of it. Hold that jack with the backing wrench and torque every joint to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m). Each stack stands 62 mm proud of SB2's front and must not carry the cable: bend the cable down from the stack's OUT to the seam bundle at the unit's lower edge and strap it (Velcro) to that bundle, or to the cable manager, within 150 mm of the stack, then on to the side lane; never lever a stack sideways. HUB-N goes down at t0 with the hub (its PoE injector's outlet is switched off); nothing RF changes. Then route every cable through the right side lane: down to the lower edge of its unit (the seam with the unit below), along it to the side of the rack, along the side and in along the lower edge of the other unit; never across the face of another box (every tile keeps 17 mm clear above and below its SMA; runs pass 15 mm or more in front). Connect tile 1 first; at the B tile torque to 8 in-lb with the backing wrench on the jack. If a seam bundle from an earlier step lies close to a tile, ease it aside by hand and fit the wrench sideways. The four cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IF link E2-W2 (30 + 1 dB pads)
steps.text: For each tile n = 1-4: pad stack PAD-E2-W2.tn screwed onto E2.N tile n (SB4.M4.Tn); cable from the stack's OUT to W2.S tile n (SB1.M4.Tn). Fit the pad stacks first, straight out to the front: BW-S30W2+ (30 dB) on the tile, then BW-S1W2+ (1 dB) on it (30 dB + 1 dB = 31 dB, target 30.7 dB, the A7 'after' setting; pad schedule); read the value printed on each pad first; each pad's male nut screws onto the female jack in front of it. Hold that jack with the backing wrench and torque every joint to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m). Each stack stands 62 mm proud of SB4's front and must not carry the cable: bend the cable down from the stack's OUT to the seam bundle at the unit's lower edge and strap it (Velcro) to that bundle, or to the cable manager, within 150 mm of the stack, then on to the side lane; never lever a stack sideways. Then route every cable through the right side lane: down to the lower edge of its unit (the seam with the unit below), along it to the side of the rack, along the side and in along the lower edge of the other unit; never across the face of another box (every tile keeps 17 mm clear above and below its SMA; runs pass 15 mm or more in front). Connect tile 1 first; at the B tile torque to 8 in-lb with the backing wrench on the jack. If a seam bundle from an earlier step lies close to a tile, ease it aside by hand and fit the wrench sideways. The four cables are one stock length (equal length, not phase-matched: assumptions); coil slack in the side lane.

steps.title: IP-50 conducted chains
steps.text: Per hop: radio (A side) -> waveguide transition (bolted to the radio flange) -> SA18S10W-30 30 dB 10 W pad -> BW-S10W2+ 10 dB pad -> ONE SMA cable (0.30 m, see the table) -> SA18S10W-30 30 dB 10 W pad -> transition -> radio (B side): 70 dB fixed, no programmable attenuator. First screw the pads onto each transition's SMA: the 30 dB 10 W pad on every transition, its input (high-power) side on the transition (if it carries an arrow, the arrow points away from the radio), then the 10 dB pad on the A side's 30 dB pad (stacks WGP-W1-CORE-A to WGP-E1-E2-B); the transition carries the stack. Torque every SMA to 8 in-lb (0.9 N m) with the SMA torque wrench while holding the jack with the backing wrench, every pad joint included. The SMA cable drops from the A-side stack to the table top and rises to the B-side stack. If the band turns out to be 23 GHz the 10 dB pad becomes a 2.92 mm 10 dB fixed attenuator DC-40 GHz (part TBC) (assumptions). The radios stay unpowered until the last stage of power-up, after every chain is complete with its pads.

steps.title: Checks and power-up
steps.text: Run the install checks (guide section 6). Before mains: every earth bond fitted and checked under 0.1 ohm (B001-B012), the GNSS arrestor bonded (B003) before its lead is on the splitter; every PDU outlet OFF with power-on state OFF (set when the PDUs were commissioned), every DC breaker OFF (the DCD1M main breaker too), every GMT fuse out, every DC load end unlanded and taped, the strip switch OFF. Then power up: PDUs (cords into WALL.S1-S3 and check every outlet reads OFF), switches and bench controller (strip cord into WALL.S4 and strip ON; switch the SW-DATA / SW-OOB / GNSS-SPL outlets ON at the front panel; wait for them to boot), servers and hosts (outlets ON; SRV-E2E first), DC rectifiers (earth bonds checked; outlets ON; meter each breaker / fuse output at its free load end before landing the load), nodes (close CB7-CB10 (box fans) first and check every fan runs; then CB1-CB6 one at a time; INJ-HUB outlet ON), radios last (GMT fuses F1-F6 in one at a time; supply outlets ON; only after every chain is complete with its pads).

power_up.detail: plug A030 into WALL.S4 and switch the strip ON: BENCH-CTL, MONITOR, SPECAN; at PDU-A's own front panel (rack rear; there is no network yet) switch ON PDU-A.O3 (SW-DATA), PDU-A.O4 (SW-OOB), PDU-A.O5 (GNSS-SPL), then set the power-on state of these outlets to ON so management survives a mains dip; wait for the switches to boot; BENCH-CTL must reach every PDU and switch over SW-OOB before the next stage

power_up.title: servers and hosts
power_up.detail: switch ON PDU-C.O2 (SRV-E2E) and wait for it to boot, so the E2E controller is up before any Terragraph unit boots; then switch ON PDU-C.O3 (SRV-DPIR), PDU-B.O4 (HOST-W1), PDU-B.O5 (HOST-W2), PDU-B.O6 (HOST-E1), PDU-B.O7 (HOST-E2), PDU-B.O8 (HOST-S), PDU-C.O1 (HOST-N), PDU-A.O6 (AGENT-W1), PDU-A.O7 (AGENT-W2), PDU-A.O8 (AGENT-E1), PDU-B.O1 (AGENT-E2), PDU-B.O2 (AGENT-S), PDU-B.O3 (AGENT-N)

power_up.title: DC rectifiers
power_up.do: earth bonds checked; outlets ON; meter each breaker / fuse output at its free load end before landing the load
power_up.detail: with the rectifiers still off, check every earth bond end to end with the meter on ohms (leads nulled), under 0.1 ohm (B001-B012); with both rectifiers off, every CB open and every GMT fuse out, meter ohms: DC-DIST + bus to DC-DIST return, + bus to RACK-EARTH and return to RACK-EARTH; DC-DIST2 bus A and bus B to RTN: each must climb to OL or above 1 Mohm (the rectifier capacitors charge first); a reading under 1 kohm is a short or an earth fault (reversed strap, nicked run): find it before switching on; DC-DIST2 RTN to RACK-EARTH must read under 0.1 ohm (positive-ground system); the +48 V system stays floating: do not bond it to earth; switch ON PDU-A.O1 (DC-RECT module 1), PDU-B.O9 (DC-RECT module 2), PDU-A.O2 (DC-RECT2); close the DCD1M main / input breaker if fitted, with every CB still open, and meter the DC-DIST bus: + bus to return +43 to +56 V; then check the earth reference with COM on RACK-EARTH: DC-DIST2 RTN reads 0 V and DC-DIST2 bus A reads -43 to -56 V; then one position at a time (CB1-CB10 and F1-F6): close the breaker (or insert the fuse), meter COM on the return (unsleeved) conductor and the red probe on the supply (sleeved) conductor at the free load end: a DC-DIST breaker output reads about +48 V (+43 to +56 V); a DC-DIST2 fuse output reads about -48 V (-43 to -56 V); a switched supply output reads about -48 V (-43 to -56 V); any other sign or value: stop, open the breaker or pull the fuse and correct the run at its supply end; open the breaker (pull the fuse with the fuse puller) again, then land the red / blue-sleeved conductor on the load's + terminal (PA adaptor, Spider DCIN plug) or -48 V pin (radio) and the unsleeved conductor on the other, torque adaptor and DCIN plug terminals to the value marked on them, push each DCIN plug into its green 4-pole DC header and tighten its flange screws, and for a radio mate the DC connector; the same for the switched supplies PDU-C.O5 (PSU-W1-CORE@CORE), PDU-C.O6 (PSU-CORE-E1@CORE): outlet ON, measure at the free radio end, outlet OFF, then land it and mate the radio's DC connector

power_up.title: nodes
power_up.do: close CB7-CB10 (box fans) first and check every fan runs; then CB1-CB6 one at a time; INJ-HUB outlet ON
power_up.detail: before closing any breaker, on the E2E controller (SRV-E2E, up since the last stage) disable ignition for the bridge links E2-W2, E1-N and W1-S (tg ignition link -n link-E2-W2 --disable, then the same for link-E1-N and link-W1-S; TG link names TBC with the lab topology) and read the setting back, so they stay down until MARL engages them after t0 (node level, from the A-end agent PC: event procedure); close DC-DIST CB7 (SB1 DCIN), CB8 (SB2 DCIN), CB9 (SB3 DCIN), CB10 (SB4 DCIN) one at a time and check that each box's fans run within 1 min (if not: open that breaker, leave the nodes of every box it feeds off and find out why); then close DC-DIST CB1 (PA-01, node W1), CB2 (PA-02, node W2), CB3 (PA-03, node S), CB4 (PA-04, node N), CB5 (PA-05, node E1), CB6 (PA-06, node E2) one at a time; switch ON PDU-C.O4 (INJ-HUB, node HUB); if a box's fans stop while its nodes boot, power that box down: SB1: CB1, CB2, then CB7; SB2: switch PDU-C.O4 OFF, then CB8; SB3: CB3, CB4, then CB9; SB4: CB5, CB6, then CB10; wait for every node to join the E2E controller; the bridges E2-W2, E1-N, W1-S stay down (ignition disabled before the first breaker): check on the E2E controller that they are not ignited and that every other link comes up on its fixed pads; then read each PDU's input current on its own display (PDU-A, PDU-B, PDU-C): each must be 12.8 A or less (80 % of 16 A); if one is above, stop and move a load

power_up.title: radios last
power_up.do: GMT fuses F1-F6 in one at a time; supply outlets ON; only after every chain is complete with its pads
power_up.detail: first confirm every IP-50 chain (W001-W012) is complete and torqued (transition bolted, a SA18S10W-30 on each transition, the BW-S10W2+ on the A side's, the one SMA cable on both stacks; no open flange or SMA); never power a radio with an open RF port; then insert the GMT fuses on DC-DIST2 one at a time: F1 (IP50-W1-CORE@W1), F2 (IP50-CORE-E1@E1), F3 (IP50-W1-W2@W1), F4 (IP50-W1-W2@W2), F5 (IP50-E1-E2@E1), F6 (IP50-E1-E2@E2); switch ON PDU-C.O5 (PSU-W1-CORE@CORE), PDU-C.O6 (PSU-CORE-E1@CORE); after 30 min check every radio's temperature in the IP-50 web UI or CLI, reached in-band over the data network from SRV-E2E (the NMS host; BENCH-CTL has no data-network port); then read each PDU's input current on its own display (PDU-A, PDU-B, PDU-C): each must be 12.8 A or less (80 % of 16 A); if one is above, stop and move a load

pad_schedule.rule: 41 dB needs more than 2 pads: nearest total 2 pads make

bridges.hold: on the E2E controller (SRV-E2E) disable ignition for the bridge links E2-W2, E1-N and W1-S (tg ignition link -n link-E2-W2 --disable, then the same for link-E1-N and link-W1-S; TG link names TBC with the lab topology) and read the setting back
bridges.engage: MARL engages a bridge at node level, with no E2E controller (SRV-E2E is off after t0): the MARL agent of the bridge's A-end node sends the Terragraph minion command tg2 minion assoc to its node (initiator = the A-end sector, responder = the B-end sector) from its agent PC, in-band over the site VLAN on SW-DATA (the nodes have no SW-OOB port): E2-W2 from AGENT-E2 (E2.N to W2.S); E1-N from AGENT-E1 (E1.N to N.W); W1-S from AGENT-W1 (W1.S to S.E). TBC: that the N367 firmware accepts a minion-level association with no controller running (open question); fallback: a standby E2E controller on BENCH-CTL (never switched), or SRV-E2E on an unswitched outlet
bridges.after: switch SRV-E2E (PDU-C.O2) ON first and wait for the E2E controller to come up; disable ignition for the bridges again (link-E2-W2, link-E1-N, link-W1-S) and read it back; a bridge MARL associated stays up: take it down from its A-end agent PC (tg2 minion dissoc, TBC) and check on the controller that every bridge is down; only then switch ON INJ-HUB (PDU-C.O4), PSU-W1-CORE@CORE (PDU-C.O5), PSU-CORE-E1@CORE (PDU-C.O6), so the hub and CORE re-join with the bridges held down; then SRV-DPIR (PDU-C.O3); let every node and radio re-join before the next run
bridges.tbc: TG link names (link-<A node>-<B node>) TBC with the lab topology; minion-level association with no E2E controller TBC on the N367 firmware (open question)
